governanceNotes: Deliberate deferral, not an authored suggestion: an isolated third, fourth, or sixth cranial-nerve palsy IS the nerve identity whose defining presentation includes binocular diplopia - the acute-diplopia cohort found 53.7% of acute-onset diplopia cases are an isolated third/fourth/sixth nerve palsy (O'Colmain 2014) - so an edge from this identity to the catalog diplopia identity would restate the diagnostic presentation (the ME-41 phenotype-identity barrier applied identically to balint-s-syndrome and common-peroneal-neuropathy).

The natural downstream candidates lack catalog identities (persistent diplopia-related functional vision loss, amblyopia from chronic strabismus, exposure keratopathy from lagophthalmos), and the palsy-etiology literature (microvascular ischemia, aneurysm, tumor, trauma, inflammation) describes causes rather than downstream outcomes; the differential-diagnosis and management literature is diagnostic/treatment-class rather than natural-history evidence, so no defensible target identity exists.
